fluff.overview: The Kallon UL-series is a family of industrial construction vehicles introduced in 3054 by Kallon Industries. Designed as affordable, versatile worksite equipment, the series quickly established itself as the benchmark for civilian construction machinery across the Inner Sphere. All four production models share an identical ten-ton tracked chassis with an adjustable-height suspension, differing only in their mounted construction apparatus. Kallon produces the UL-series at multiple facilities across the rimward Inner Sphere, with plants in both the Federated Suns and Free Worlds League fabricating all components onsite. The vehicles are light enough to transport by truck, making them popular with construction firms operating on remote frontier worlds far from established infrastructure.
fluff.capabilities:
The UL-series chassis features an innovative adjustable-height design built around hydraulic outriggers mounted on the drive tracks. These outriggers lift the main body above obstacles and allow the vehicle to operate on hillsides or span narrow pits. An automatic leveling sensor tied to an audible alarm ensures stable operation on uneven terrain. The Kallon Growler internal combustion engine provides sufficient torque to drive any of the four available construction attachments, and a half-ton fuel tank gives the vehicles extended operational range without refueling, a strong selling point for companies breaking new ground far from support facilities.

At ten tons, the UL-series is light enough for truck transport, a significant advantage for construction companies working at remote sites. The tracked chassis carries only minimal industrial-grade plating rated to deflect debris rather than weapons fire, offering no meaningful protection in a combat environment. The vehicles mount no weapons and rely entirely on their operators and local site security for defense.
fluff.deployment: The UL-14 is a dual-blade bulldozer mounting heavy blades on both the front and rear of the chassis. This configuration allows the vehicle to work in both directions without needing to turn around, increasing operator productivity. Many operators consider this a significant profit-earning feature, and it has endeared the UL-14 to construction company executives. The UL-14 is commonly paired with UL-11 Rock Cutters at demolition and site clearing operations.
fluff.history:
Kallon Industries introduced the UL-series in 3054 to compete in the civilian construction equipment market, a sector where larger firms like Earthwerks Incorporated had established footholds with products such as the Lesseps Dumper line. The series found rapid commercial success across the rimward Inner Sphere, with Kallon factories in the Federated Suns and Free Worlds League producing all four models using entirely onsite-manufactured components. Minor regional variations in weights and measures exist between production facilities, but the core designs remain identical.

Kallon executives have aggressively marketed the vehicles through demonstrations showing UL units clearing debris from burning structures and responding to vehicle accidents. This campaign directly targets Earthwerks, whose own construction equipment supplements have suffered from the poor reputation of the Lesseps Dumper among operators. The strategy has proven effective, allowing Kallon to capture a growing share of the civilian construction market that Earthwerks has struggled to defend.
